title: Release images built on a floating runner with an x86-64-v3 default compiler crashed with SIGILL on CPUs without AVX

source.reference: kaniop 0.23.0 images (kaniop, kaniop-crd-migrator, kaniop-webhook, kaniop-data-mover) died with SIGILL (exit 132) on an Intel Atom C2000: AVX instructions in AWS-LC CPU detection before main and in vendored OpenSSL on the first TLS operation. Release images were built natively on runs-on: ubuntu-latest, which moved to ubuntu-26.04 whose GCC defaults to -march=x86-64-v3; the cc crate adds no -march, so aws-lc-sys and openssl-src were compiled for AVX2. PR CI builds on ubuntu-24.04 and never ran a binary on an old CPU, so nothing caught it. Reproduced with qemu-x86_64 -cpu Westmere (0.23.0 exit 132, 0.21.1 exit 0).

commands: .ci/check-x86-64-baseline.sh <directory with the 0.23.0 binaries> (must fail with SIGILL)
required_properties: The explanation names the root cause: the C dependencies (aws-lc-sys, openssl-src) inherit the build host compiler's default -march, and the floating ubuntu-latest runner moved to an image whose GCC defaults to x86-64-v3; Rust code is not the cause
Every workflow that builds shipped x86_64 binaries compiles C code for the baseline, for example with CFLAGS_x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu=-march=x86-64, without changing the aarch64 build
The release image runner is pinned to an explicit image instead of ubuntu-latest
CI runs every shipped x86_64 binary on an emulated CPU without AVX (for example qemu-x86_64 -cpu Westmere) before the images are pushed, and fails on SIGILL
The data mover check performs a real TLS request (for example against a local openssl s_server), because --version does not reach the vendored OpenSSL code
The guard is proved to fail on the 0.23.0 binaries and to pass on the 0.21.1 binaries
PR CI runs the production release-profile compatibility check as part of a mandatory status check; PR and release use the same portable build userspace even when the host is Ubuntu 26.04 amd64v3
The publishing job uses the checked x86_64 binaries without rebuilding them on the host; the arm64 path is unaffected

Automatic release tags are created only after the exact master commit has passed Rust CI and produced a verified x86 release artifact; both latest and versioned image publishing consume that artifact rather than compiling or running the baseline probe again.
forbidden_changes: Pin only the runner without forcing a baseline -march, leaving the build dependent on the next image's compiler default
Rely on RUSTFLAGS -C target-cpu, which does not reach C code built by the cc crate, or disable the AWS-LC/OpenSSL assembly instead of fixing the C compiler target
Check only --version or --help for the data mover
Treat any non-zero exit as a guard failure, so a binary that rejects the dummy input is reported as a CPU incompatibility, or treat any exit as success so SIGILL passes
Run the emulated guest against the Ubuntu amd64v3 host loader or replace verified binaries with a subsequent native host rebuild
Create a tag before the master compatibility job succeeds, or rebuild x86 release binaries on the tag workflow if a verified artifact is missing.
